title: Constant Rate of Change and d = rt
seo_title: Grade 7 Constant Rate of Change and d = rt Worksheets (TEKS 7.4A, STAAR)
standard_text: 7.4A represent constant rates of change in mathematical and real-world problems given pictorial, tabular, verbal, numeric, graphical, and algebraic representations, including d = rt
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 worksheets for Texas TEKS 7.4A: d = rt for distance, rate and time, constant rates of change in tables and graphs, and unit rates. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Rate of change = change in y ÷ change in x.
key_sub: d = rt: 60 mi/h for 2.5 h is 150 miles.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A constant rate of change means y changes by the same amount each time x goes up by 1.
  • Rate of change = change in y ÷ change in x.
  • For motion at a constant speed, use d = rt (distance = rate × time). Then r = d ÷ t and t = d ÷ r.
  • On a graph, a constant rate of change is a straight line.

Examples

Example

60 mi/h for 2.5 hours

d = 60 × 2.5

Answer: 150 miles

Example

Hours 1, 2, 3; miles 45, 90, 135

(90 − 45) ÷ (2 − 1)

Answer: 45 miles per hour

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Multiplying when you should divideTo find r, divide: r = d ÷ t.
Mixing up minutes and hoursChange 30 minutes to 0.5 hour first.
Reading the rate from one pair onlyUse the change in y ÷ change in x.

faq.q: Is a rate of change the same as a unit rate?
faq.a: Yes, when it is the change for 1 unit of x.

faq.q: How do I see a constant rate on a graph?
faq.a: The points lie on a straight line.

items.e: The line goes through (0, 0). Slope = y ÷ x = 3 ÷ 1 = 3 pages per minute.

items.q: Which equation shows a proportional relationship?
items.e: A proportional relationship goes through (0, 0): y = kx with no + b. The answer is y = 4x.
